content.jointProblem: Can a lightweight content-based or hybrid product-page recommender outperform best-seller sorting for one Harmat client with only 500–2,000 transactions, and under what conditions would cross-client transfer help rather than harm? The first experiment would compare best-seller, category-based, content-based and simple hybrid baselines using chronological holdouts, testing recommendation relevance and coverage before considering transfer from any legally available, compatible source.

rationale.text: Prodanović has directly studied recommendation under population shift, providing relevant expertise for assessing whether information from other stores could help rather than simply pooling their transactions.

sources.quote: We study unsupervised domain adaptation for GRU-based session encoders
We conduct ablations separating the contributions of the encoder adversarial loss and a category-level alignment auxiliary objective.

rationale.text: Her work addresses differences between product catalogues and investigates category embeddings as a bridge, relevant to evaluating transfer between heterogeneous client stores.

sources.quote: Retail datasets from different markets differ not only in user behaviour but also in the item catalogue, making direct feature-level comparison impossible.
catalogue-embedding alignment—using pre-trained product category embeddings as a bridge—degrades most gracefully

rationale.text: She can contribute evaluation design that guards against temporal leakage and misleading transfer gains, important when a small dataset leaves little room for independent validation.

sources.quote: including temporal leakage across domain boundaries, conflation of domain shift with concept drift
For each pitfall we propose a concrete corrective protocol.

rationale.text: She has practical retail prediction consulting experience, including evaluation, calibration and decisions about retraining.

sources.quote: on the evaluation and calibration of their in-house next-basket prediction system, advising specifically on retraining triggers and population segmentation.

constraints.text: The experiment must work within the existing sparse transaction history rather than depend on collecting a substantially larger dataset, and must compare against best-seller sorting.

sources.quote: The largest dataset had 1 900 completed orders over eighteen months; the smallest had around 520.
We do not have the budget or the traffic to wait for larger datasets.
Simple best-seller sorting actually outperformed the model in our A/B test

constraints.text: Data access must be covered by a data-sharing agreement and remain within the permitted use of anonymised transaction and catalogue records; access does not itself establish permission for cross-client pooling.

sources.quote: access to anonymised client datasets under a data-sharing agreement.
We can give a collaborator full read access to anonymised transaction and product catalogue data.

constraints.text: Scope should remain a one-client prototype with limited integration demands, matching the company's allocation of roughly one developer-day per week.

sources.quote: A working prototype for one client would be enough to start.
We can allocate one mid-level developer for roughly one day per week to an applied research collaboration

constraints.text: Widget integration must account for the company's client-VPS deployment environment, and user-facing strings must follow its three-language review process; specific runtime resources remain to be agreed.

sources.quote: Docker for containerised deployments on client VPS environments
we test every user-facing string in all three languages before a build ships

constraints.text: Research compute cannot be treated as dedicated or unlimited; any GPU-heavy extension must account for the group's shared cluster capacity.

sources.quote: Her group's GPU cluster capacity is currently shared with two other research groups
may be a bottleneck for very large-scale experiments without additional infrastructure support from a partner.

risks: The researcher's recommendation studies use much larger session or transaction datasets. Their results do not establish effectiveness with 500–2,000 orders; the first experiment must test performance in this actual low-data regime before adopting complex adaptation.

Session-based next-item and next-basket prediction differ from recommendations on a product page. Available order logs may lack browsing sessions or stable customer identifiers; the first experiment must establish what prediction target the data genuinely support.

Product-description modelling and multilingual content recommendations are not directly validated by the supplied research evidence. The first content-based baseline must test description completeness, language handling and category consistency.

Cross-client transfer could cause negative transfer when assortments and purchasing behaviour differ. Compatible source data and permission to reuse them are not established; transfer may need to be excluded entirely.
Low traffic may make a conversion-based A/B test inconclusive within an affordable period. Offline improvements would not establish commercial benefit.
The researcher's availability and the company's cash budget, deadline, VPS resources and acceptable latency are unknown. Shared compute and limited developer time could delay delivery.
questions: Can Prodanović confirm availability, a named delivery contact and an achievable schedule for a scoped joint project?
Which client will host the prototype, and what cash budget, delivery deadline and maintenance ownership can Harmat commit?
Do records include timestamps, line items, quantities, stable anonymised customer identifiers, impressions or browsing sessions? How many products and repeat purchases are represented?
How complete are descriptions, categories and attributes, and which languages appear in the selected catalogue? Are historical catalogue and stock states available for leakage-safe evaluation?
What recommendation behaviour should the widget prioritise—substitutes, complements or discovery—and what improvement over best-sellers would be commercially meaningful?
Can the previous A/B-test design and results be reviewed, and what traffic and instrumentation are available for a prospective test?
Does the data-sharing agreement permit cross-client model training or use of external source models and datasets, and what retention, access and deletion rules apply?
What VPS memory, CPU, latency and integration limits apply, and should recommendations be precomputed rather than generated on request?
